docs.title: Project
docs.text: Project registration is the first main step. A project is the main record for your work, and one project can contain one or more studies.

docs.title: Register Project
docs.text:
Purpose: Tell IMDA what the project is about, who is responsible, and how the work was funded.

Use Register Project from the left sidebar. Complete the project form first, because the Project ID is required before creating the study, sample, and experiment records.

docs.title: Project Form Screen
docs.text: In the project form, fill all required fields and select the research area that best matches the submitted work.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text:
Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Name of the overall project. Use a clear title that tells what the project is about. Avoid very short titles. Project Contributors* Principal Investigator, submitter, and other responsible people. Enter full name, email, and institution wherever requested. Do not use initials only. Research Area* Subject area of the project. Select the closest option available in the portal. Funding Source* Funding agency, grant number, or institutional support. Use the official funder name and grant number if available. Project Description* Short description of the aim and type of data. Write 3-5 simple sentences.

Minimum Detail

The project should clearly show who is responsible for the data. Use complete names, valid email addresses, and full institution names.

Project vs Study

The Project is the overall work. The Study is the specific experiment or dataset inside that project. One project can contain multiple studies, so create separate studies when the experiment, sample set, method, or dataset is different.

Common Mistakes

Avoid short titles such as only the disease name or instrument name. Do not leave contributor, research area, or funding details incomplete when they are known.

Final Action:

  1. Fill all fields marked with an asterisk.
  2. Select the closest Research Area.
  3. Check the funding source and project description carefully.
  4. Click Submit to create the Project ID.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Use this page as a quick checklist before starting a real IMDA submission. Keep your project details, sample details, experiment files, and raw data files ready before you begin.

IMDA Portal

Use the live IMDA portal for submission: https://ibdc.dbt.gov.in/imda/home.html.

docs.title: Template Files to Fill
docs.text:
Download and review these Excel templates before filling the portal forms. These files tell users what sample and experiment details must be prepared.

Template Use This For Key Details to Prepare Sample template Sample registration. Sample name, sample type, sample preparation method, extraction method, treatment/condition, replicate details, storage condition, and number of files per sample. MS experiment template Mass spectrometry experiment registration. Sample ID, sample name, reference standard, chromatography details, MS instrument, ionization method, ion mode/scan polarity, transformation software, and raw data file details. NMR experiment template NMR experiment registration. Sample ID, sample name, reference standard, NMR instrument, NMR type, experiment type, frequency, probe, solvent, tube size, and transformation software.

Prepare Before Portal Entry

Fill the sample template first. After sample registration, IMDA will give sample IDs. Copy those sample IDs exactly into the MS or NMR experiment template.

docs.title: Data and File Preparation
docs.text:
• Keep the raw data files from the instrument ready.
  • Keep processed/result files ready, if available.
  • Compress large raw data folders into individual ZIP files before upload.
  • Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and dots in file names.
  • Do not use spaces or special characters in file names.
  • Organize raw data into clear local folders before compression.
  • Install an FTP client such as FileZilla.
  • Use open file formats where possible. IMDA prefers mzML for MS data and nmrML for NMR data.

docs.title: Information to Keep Ready
docs.text:
• Collect name, email, and affiliation details for the Principal Investigator and all contributing authors.
  • Prepare the study summary, keywords, DOI where applicable, and ethical or institutional approval numbers.
  • Use the same project name, study name, sample names, method names, and file names in all forms and templates.

Before Moving Ahead

Do not upload files until the project, study, sample, and experiment forms are complete. The file upload step depends on the IDs created in the earlier steps.

docs.title: After Login: User Dashboard
docs.text: After login, the dashboard is the main page where users can check their submitted data and continue the submission workflow.

docs.title: What This Page Shows
docs.text:
Dashboard Area What Users Can See or Do Left sidebar Shows the submission order under Submit New Data. Users should follow this order: Register Project, Register Study, Register Sample, Zip and MD5 Checksum, Register Experiment, FTP Files Upload, Map Uploaded Files, and Submitted Data. Top tabs Opens different user records such as My Data, My Project, My Study, Authors, My Sample, Experiment, Accession List, and Submit New Data. Summary boxes Shows quick counts for uploaded projects, studies, samples, experiments, and files. This helps users confirm what has already been added. Submitted data table Shows the user's submitted study records, including Project ID, Study ID, Study Title, Study Type, Date of Submission, and metabolite/compound file status.

How to Use This Page

First check the left sidebar to understand the submission order. Then use the dashboard table to confirm whether your project, study, experiment, and uploaded files are visible in your account.

docs.title: Experiment
docs.text: Experiment registration tells IMDA how the samples were measured and which experiment/result files belong to the selected study.

docs.title: Experiment Form Screen
docs.text: Use Register Experiment from the left sidebar. Select the technique, select the correct study, upload the metabolite/compound file, and upload the completed MS or NMR experiment template.

docs.title: What to Fill in the Portal
docs.text: Portal Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Select Technique* Select the experiment technique, such as MS or NMR. Choose the same technique used in the study and template. Study Select the Study ID linked to this experiment. Make sure the selected study belongs to the correct project. Metabolite / Compound File Upload the raw, processed, or annotated metabolite/compound result file when available. Use a clear file name and keep the same name in later file mapping. MS/NMR File Template Upload the completed MS or NMR Excel template. Use MS template for mass spectrometry and NMR template for nuclear magnetic resonance. Do not change column headers.

docs.title: Where to Get Sample IDs
docs.text:
After sample registration, open My Sample to view the generated Sample ID values. These IDs must be copied into the first column, Sample id, in both the MS and NMR experiment templates.

Sample ID Rule

Do not type local sample names in the Sample id column. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID exactly as shown in My Sample. If one sample has multiple data files, repeat the same Sample ID once for each file row. For example, if Sample ID 1060 has 2 files, enter 1060 in two rows and give the correct file name/checksum for each row.

docs.title: MS Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the MS file template when the study uses mass spectrometry. Fill one row for each sample/file combination.

Use Dropdown Values

In the MS template, columns such as Mass Spectrometer Type, MS Instrument Name, MS Instrument Type, MS Ionization Method, and Ion Mode/Scan Polarity have dropdown options. Select the closest correct value from the dropdown. Use Others only when the correct instrument or method is not available in the list.

MS Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample id First column in the MS template. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID from My Sample exactly. Sample Name Sample name used in the sample template. Reference Standard Reference standard or internal standard used. Enter NA if not applicable. Chromatography Instrument Name LC/GC/CE or other chromatography system used before MS. Column Model Chromatography column model/name. Column Type Column chemistry/type, such as C18, HILIC, GC column, or NA. Mass Spectrometer Type Select from the dropdown, such as LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS, MALDI-TOF, Tandem MS, or the closest available type. MS Instrument Name Select the instrument model/name from the dropdown list. Example options include ABI Sciex, Agilent, Bruker, Thermo, Waters, Shimadzu, and other instrument entries. MS Instrument Type Select from the dropdown, such as Triple TOF, TOF, QTOF, Orbitrap, FT-ICR-MS, Single quadrupole, Triple quadrupole, or Others. MS Ionization Method Select from the dropdown, such as ESI, nano ESI, APCI, APPI, MALDI, EI, CI, FAB, DIOS, or Others. Ion Mode/Scan Polarity Select from the dropdown: Positive, Negative, or Positive;Negative. Data Transformation(Software/s Used) Software used for conversion/processing, such as ProteoWizard, XCMS, MZmine, vendor software, or NA. MS Data File Name Exact raw/ZIP data file name that will be uploaded. Include the extension. Md5checksum MD5 checksum for the final uploaded MS data file. Generate it after the ZIP/file is final.

Multiple Files for One Sample

If Number of files per sample is 2, create 2 rows for that sample in the MS template. Repeat the same Sample id and enter the matching MS Data File Name and Md5checksum for each file.

docs.title: NMR Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the NMR file template when the study uses nuclear magnetic resonance. Fill one row for each sample/file combination.

Use Dropdown Values

In the NMR template, columns such as NMR Instrument Name, NMR Type, NMR Experiment Type, and NMR Solvent have dropdown options. Select the closest correct value from the dropdown. Use Others only when the correct solvent or option is not available in the list.

NMR Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample id First column in the NMR template. Copy the IMDA-generated Sample ID from My Sample exactly. Sample Name Sample name used in the sample template. Reference Standard Reference standard used for NMR. Enter NA if not applicable. NMR Instrument Name Select the instrument model/name from the dropdown list. Example options include Bruker and Jeol NMR instrument entries. NMR Type Select from the dropdown: Solution NMR or Solid State NMR. NMR Experiment Type Select from the dropdown, such as 1D 1H, 1D 13C, 1D 31P, 2D experiments, or the closest available option. NMR Spectrometer Frequency Spectrometer frequency, such as 400 MHz, 500 MHz, or 600 MHz. NMR Probe Probe used for acquisition. NMR Probe Temperature Probe/sample temperature during acquisition, with unit where possible. NMR Solvent Select from the dropdown, such as CCL4, CS2, CDCL3, C6D6, D2O, Acetone, DMSO, Methanol, Ethanol, or Others. NMR Tube Size Tube size, such as 5 mm, or NA if not applicable. Data Transformation(Software/s Used) Software used for processing/conversion. NMR Data File Name Exact raw/ZIP NMR data file name that will be uploaded. Include the extension. Md5checksum MD5 checksum for the final uploaded NMR data file. Generate it after the ZIP/file is final.

Multiple Files for One Sample

If Number of files per sample is 2, create 2 rows for that sample in the NMR template. Repeat the same Sample id and enter the matching NMR Data File Name and Md5checksum for each file.

docs.title: Match IDs and File Names
docs.text:
1. Use the Sample IDs shown in My Sample after sample registration.
  2. Use the correct template for the selected technique.
  3. If one sample has multiple files, repeat the same Sample ID in multiple rows, one row per file.
  4. Keep uploaded file names exactly the same as the file names entered in the template.
  5. Generate the MD5 checksum only after the final file or ZIP is ready.
  6. Use NA for required fields that are genuinely not applicable.

Common Mistakes

Do not use local sample names where IMDA expects Sample IDs. Do not rename template headers. Make sure technique, Study ID, file name, and MD5 checksum all match the final uploaded files.

Final Action:

  1. Download the correct MS or NMR template.
  2. Fill the template using Sample IDs and exact file names.
  3. Calculate MD5 checksum for each final uploaded file.
  4. Upload the metabolite/compound file and the completed MS/NMR template.
  5. Click Submit.

docs.title: FTP File Uploads
docs.text:
Use the FTP login details provided by IMDA to upload your zipped data files.

Detail Purpose HOSTNAME, USERNAME, PASSWORD Login details for FTP upload. Project Folder Select the project folder first. Study Folder Select the correct study folder before uploading files. Instruction Note Read the warning shown on the portal before upload.

docs.title: FileZilla Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open FileZilla or another FTP client.
  2. Enter the host, username, and password from the portal.
  3. Navigate to the project folder.
  4. Open the correct study folder.
  5. Upload all zipped raw data files and processed/result files.

Common Mistakes

Do not upload files into the wrong project or study folder. Do not upload incomplete folders when the SOP requires a ZIP file, and do not change file names after generating the MD5 checksum.

docs.title: Map Uploaded Files
docs.text:
Mapping means telling IMDA which uploaded file belongs to which study and sample.

Mapping Field What to Select or Enter Study ID Study under which the file was uploaded. Uploaded File Exact file transferred through FTP. Sample ID Correct IMDA sample ID connected to that file. Protocol / Assay Method used to generate the file. MD5 Checksum Lowercase checksum value generated before upload. Finalize Submission Use only after all files are mapped and verified.

Mapping Requirement

Each uploaded file must be linked to the correct study, sample, method, and checksum. Do not finalize the submission if any file is missing or linked to the wrong sample.

  1. Open Map Uploaded Files from the IMDA sidebar.
  2. Verify that all uploaded files appear under the correct Study ID.
  3. Link each file to the correct sample ID and protocol.
  4. Enter the matching MD5 checksum.
  5. Confirm every sample has its corresponding raw and/or processed data file.
  6. Click Validate All Files For This Study only after checking all forms and file links.

Before Final Submit

After the final submit/check step, some edit options may disappear. Check all details before clicking the final button.

docs.title: Final Submission Check
docs.text:
Before clicking Validate All Files For This Study, confirm the following:

  • All expected raw files and processed/result files are uploaded.
  • Every uploaded file is mapped to the correct study and sample.
  • File names match the experiment template exactly.
  • MD5 checksum values match the final uploaded ZIP files.
  • The metabolite/compound file and MS/NMR template are already uploaded in Register Experiment.

docs.title: Login / Register
docs.text: Register and log in before starting a data submission.

docs.title: Where to Login or Register
docs.text:
Open the IMDA portal and use the top-right links to access Login or User Registration. To log in, click Login, enter the registered username and password, complete the reCAPTCHA, and click Login.

Option User Action Purpose User Registration Open User Registration. Creates the account required for data submission. Login Open Login. Starts an authenticated session for submission and dashboard access. Submit Open Submit Data after login. Opens the new data submission workflow.

docs.title: User Registration Form
docs.text: Fill all mandatory fields marked with an asterisk. Use an active email address because account activation and IMDA communication will go to this email. Scroll inside the image box to view the full form.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text:
Field What to Enter Username* Login name for the IMDA portal. Use only allowed characters. Email* Active email address for account activation and IMDA communication. First name / Last name* Full user name. Do not use initials only. Organization name* Full institution or organization name. Designation* Select the closest role, such as Research Scholar, Principal Investigator, Scientist, or other available option. Password / Confirmation* Enter and confirm a password that follows the portal rules. Country* Select the user's country. State Select the state when available. ORCID Enter ORCID if the user has one. Leave blank if not available.

After registration, check the registered email for the account activation link. If login fails because the account is not active, use Resend activation link to admin on the login page.

Common Mistakes

Use an active email address, because account activation and IMDA messages depend on it. Enter the full organization name and complete first and last name instead of initials.

docs.title: Edit Profile
docs.text:
After login, users can open Profile from the top menu. Click Edit Profile to update details such as name, email, organization, designation, ORCID, and country when corrections are needed.

Before Starting Submission

Make sure the user profile has the correct full name, email address, organization name, designation, and country. These details help IMDA identify the submitter and contact the right person if clarification is needed.

docs.title: MD5 Checksum
docs.text:
Generate MD5 checksums before uploading data files. The checksum works like a file fingerprint and helps IMDA confirm that the uploaded file is the same as the file on your computer.

Access the Tool: IMDA MD5 Checksum Tool.

docs.title: What to Prepare
docs.text:
File Type What to Prepare Rule Raw data file Instrument output from MS or NMR. Compress complex folders into ZIP files before upload. Processed/result file Processed output generated from raw data. Keep names consistent with the experiment template. Metadata template Sample and experiment Excel files. File names in templates must match uploaded files exactly. Checksum file md5sum.txt generated by the IMDA script. Use the checksum matching each uploaded file.

File Naming

File names should refer to actual files, not folder names or web links. Keep the full extension visible, for example .mzML, .raw, .d.zip, .raw.zip, .csv, or .txt.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Download the script for Windows, macOS, or Linux.
  2. Run the script in the directory containing the raw data files.
  3. Confirm that the script generates md5sum.txt.
  4. Use the checksum values from md5sum.txt during file mapping.

Checksum Rules

Enter MD5 checksum values in lowercase and make sure each checksum corresponds to the exact ZIP file uploaded.

docs.title: How to Calculate MD5
docs.text:
Use the IMDA MD5 tool/script when possible. The usual steps are:

  1. Keep the final ZIP/raw file in one folder.
  2. Run the downloaded MD5 script in that same folder.
  3. Open the generated md5sum.txt file.
  4. Copy the checksum value for the exact file uploaded to IMDA.

If users need to calculate MD5 manually, they can use the command for their operating system.

Operating System Command Example What Users Should Copy Windows PowerShell Get-FileHash .\filename.zip -Algorithm MD5 Copy the value shown under Hash. Windows Command Prompt certutil -hashfile filename.zip MD5 Copy the 32-character MD5 value. macOS md5 filename.zip Copy the value printed after MD5 (...) =. Linux md5sum filename.zip Copy the first 32-character value before the file name.

Replace filename.zip with the real final file name. If the file name has spaces, place it in quotes, for example md5sum "sample raw data.zip".

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
8b1a9953c4611296a827abf8c47804d7  sample_data.zip

In this example, enter only:

8b1a9953c4611296a827abf8c47804d7

Do not copy the file name into the MD5 checksum field.

Common Mistakes

Generate the checksum after the final ZIP file is ready. If you rename, edit, re-zip, or replace a file, generate the checksum again.

docs.title: Reviewer Access URL
docs.text:
Use the reviewer access URL to share a private study record with journal reviewers or collaborators before public release.

Action: Open the submitted study details and locate URLs to Share Study Records.

docs.title: What to Check Before Sharing
docs.text: Item Check Study record Confirm that the correct study is selected. Study details Check project, study, sample, method, and file details. Uploaded files Confirm that raw and processed files are mapped correctly. Reviewer URL Copy the activated URL from the portal.

docs.title: Security Rate-Limit Policy
docs.text:
• Only 5 unique individuals can access the shared link within a 24-hour period.
  • If the limit is reached, additional users must wait until the 24-hour window resets.

docs.title: Generate the Secure Link
docs.text:
1. Click Activate Link.
  2. Use Copy to copy the URL.
  3. Share the URL with the journal editor or reviewer.

Common Mistakes

Confirm the correct study before sharing the reviewer link. Share the link only with the intended reviewer or editor because access is limited.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text: Sample registration tells IMDA what samples were used and how many files belong to each sample.

docs.title: Sample Form Screen
docs.text: Use Register Sample from the left sidebar. Select the correct study, enter the sample source and organism details, download the sample template, complete it, and upload the filled template.

docs.title: What to Fill
docs.text: Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Select Study* Study ID to which these samples belong. Choose the correct study before uploading the template. Source* Where the sample came from, such as tissue, cell line, biofluid, plant part, or culture. Use the closest term available in the portal. Avoid local short forms. Organism Name* Scientific organism name. Use binomial name, for example Homo sapiens or Oryza sativa. Taxonomy ID* NCBI taxonomy number fetched by the system. Check that the number matches the organism name. Additional Information Disease/condition, organism part, cell type, treatment, collection site, or other useful sample details. Use clear terms; enter NA only when the field does not apply. Sample File Template* Completed sample Excel template. Do not change column names in the template.

docs.title: Sample Template Columns
docs.text:
Download the Sample file template, fill one row for each sample, and upload the completed Excel file in Sample File Template. Do not rename, delete, or reorder the columns.

Template Column What the User Should Fill Sample Name Unique sample name used by the submitter. Use the same sample name later in the MS/NMR experiment template. Sample Type Type of sample, such as plasma, serum, urine, tissue, leaf, root, extract, culture, or cell line. Sample Preparation Protocol Short description of how the sample was prepared before extraction or analysis. Extraction Protocol Solvent, method, or protocol used to extract metabolites from the sample. Experimental Condition (Treated/Untreated, Healthy/Diseased, Others) Condition or group for the sample, such as treated, untreated, control, diseased, healthy, exposed, or other study group. Time of treatment Treatment duration or collection time point, such as 0 h, 24 h, 7 days, or NA if not applicable. Variant/Variety Strain, cultivar, variety, genotype, breed, or variant where applicable. Use NA if not applicable. Gender Male, female, pooled, mixed, not recorded, or NA depending on the sample type. Age Age of organism or subject, including unit where possible, such as 8 weeks, 45 days, adult, or NA. Replicates Replicate number or replicate group, such as R1, R2, R3, biological replicate 1, or pooled. Storage Conditions How the sample was stored before analysis, such as -80°C, liquid nitrogen, 4°C, room temperature, or NA. Number of files per sample Exact number of raw/processed data files that belong to that sample. This number should match the files uploaded later.

After template submission, IMDA generates sample IDs. Use those IDs in the experiment template.

Required Sample Context

Each sample should clearly connect to one study and one source. Check the study, sample name, organism name, taxonomy ID, and source before submitting.

Final Action:

  1. Download and complete the sample file template.
  2. Upload it using Choose File.
  3. Click Submit to register sample metadata.

Common Mistakes

Do not change template column headers. Check that the selected Study ID is correct, taxonomy ID matches the organism name, and required template cells use NA only when the value is genuinely not applicable.

docs.title: Study
docs.text:
Study registration explains the specific experiment or dataset. Each study must be linked to a project.

What to do: Select the correct Project ID, then fill Study Details and Author List.

One Project, Multiple Studies

One project can contain multiple studies. Create a new study under the same project when the experiment, sample set, method, or dataset is different.

docs.title: Study Form Screen
docs.text: Use Register Study from the left sidebar. Select the correct project first, then complete the study details and author list. Scroll inside the image box to view the full form.

docs.title: Study Details
docs.text:
Field What to Enter Writing Guideline Title* Title of the experiment or dataset. Include organism, sample type, and method where possible. Study Type* Technology used, such as Mass Spectrometry (MS) or Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Select the closest option in the portal. Data Type / Summary Whether the study is targeted, semi-targeted, or untargeted, plus a short summary. Write 3-5 simple sentences. Do not paste a long manuscript abstract. Keywords Important words that help others find the study. Use 3-8 keywords, such as organism, disease/condition, sample type, method, or metabolite class. Release Date* Date on which the data can become publicly available. Use the required portal date format. Publication / Approval DOI, PubMed ID, manuscript status, IEC/IBSC approval, or institutional approval number. Enter official numbers exactly as issued. If not available, use the portal's allowed option.

Study Summary

The summary should tell a new reader what was studied, which organism/sample was used, which method was used, and what data was generated.

docs.title: Author List
docs.text:
Click Add Author to include all contributors. Check names, emails, and affiliations because these details support final attribution.

Field What to Enter Name Full contributor name as it should appear in attribution. Avoid initials only. Email Active institutional or professional email address. Affiliation Department, institute, city, and country where requested. Use the full organization name. Role Select the person's role, such as PI, submitter, author, or other available option.

Final Action: Click Submit. The portal creates a Study ID, such as IMS_xxxxxx.

Common Mistakes

Do not repeat the project title as the study title unless it describes the exact experiment. Make sure the summary, keywords, data type, release date, and author details are complete before submitting.

docs.title: Submitted Data
docs.text: Use Submitted Data to check whether your study has been submitted, reviewed, corrected, or released.

docs.title: Tracking Your Study
docs.text:
1. Review the table for Project ID, Study ID, Study Title, and Date of Submission.
  2. Open the Study ID or row details to view full information and current status.
  3. Use the final IMP_xxxxxx and IMS_xxxxxx IDs for citation after release.
Status Meaning Action Required Submitted Your study has been submitted and is waiting for IMDA review. No action unless IMDA contacts you. In Review IMDA team is checking your study details and files. Check registered email frequently. Public Study is released for download. Cite the final project and study IDs.

After Submission

IMDA reviews submissions after the final submit/check step. Check the registered email for any correction request.

docs.title: Corrections After Submission
docs.text:
Use Edit File Data only when study details or uploaded files need correction before final submit/check, or when IMDA asks for a correction.

Submission Status Edit Button Status Required Action Pre-Submission Active Click the edit option for the relevant row. Post-Submission Disabled or hidden Contact IMDA support to request temporary edit access.

Common edit actions include:

  • Edit Project / Study / Sample Details: Correct project, study, or sample information before final submit/check.
  • Edit Upload Run: Replace corrupted or incorrect raw data files.
  • Edit Metabolite / Compound File: Replace the processed metabolite summary file.

docs.title: Edit Upload Run
docs.text:
Use Edit Upload Run when a raw data file needs correction or replacement.

Field What to Enter Study Select the study linked to the uploaded run. FTP Filename Select the uploaded file that needs correction. MD5 Checksum Enter the corrected lowercase checksum for the replacement file.

docs.title: Edit Metabolite / Compound File
docs.text:
Use this option when the processed metabolite or compound file needs to be replaced.

Field What to Enter Study Select the study linked to the processed file. Compound Document Upload the corrected metabolite or compound file.

docs.title: Controlled Vocabulary Updates
docs.text:
Use Browse Lists to check whether an organism, source, or MS/NMR instrument name is already available in IMDA. If the required name is missing, use Update List to request it.

Browse List What to Check MS Instrument Confirm whether the required mass spectrometry instrument already exists. NMR Instrument Confirm whether the required NMR instrument already exists. Source / Organism Terms Use existing portal terms wherever possible.

docs.title: Update List
docs.text:
Request a new list value only when the required value is not already available.

Field What to Enter List Type Select the category to update, such as MS instrument, NMR instrument, organism, or source. Name / Value Enter the exact term to be added.

docs.title: Support and Citation
docs.text:
Item Guidance Repository Indian Metabolome Data Archive (IMDA) of the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC). Project ID Use the assigned IMP_xxxxxx ID. Study ID Use the assigned IMS_xxxxxx ID. Support Email Contact imdasupport@ibdc.rcb.res.in for assistance.

Common Mistakes

Do not assume the submission is complete only because files were uploaded. Check the status in Submitted Data and respond quickly if IMDA requests corrections.
